records.central_claim: Ulama—especially ulama de cadera in Sinaloa—is a living, endangered descendant/tradition of the pre-Hispanic Mesoamerican ballgame. The wider ballgame tradition has archaeological evidence reaching at least the second millennium BCE (including a formal court dated about 1650 BCE), so describing the tradition as roughly 3,400–3,500 years old is reasonable; that dating should not be presented as proof that today’s ulama has remained unchanged for that entire period.
